gaps.sentence: Let me ___ a look at that cut on your arm.
gaps.explanation: take a look (at something) is the fixed collocation for examining something briefly.

gaps.sentence: I would never ___ advice from someone I don't respect.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'advice' from the receiver's side
gaps.explanation: take advice from somebody means to accept and follow it; the adviser gives advice.

gaps.sentence: It ___ no difference whether we leave today or tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Make no difference' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ interest on the money it borrows.
gaps.explanation: pay interest is the standard financial collocation.

gaps.sentence: I was nearly late, but I managed to ___ the last bus.
gaps.hint: to get on a bus or train in time
gaps.explanation: catch a bus/train means to arrive in time to board it; the words 'managed to' and 'nearly late' show success.

gaps.sentence: The storm ___ a lot of damage to the roof.
gaps.explanation: do damage to something is the collocation; past tense 'did' is needed here.

gaps.sentence: I only ___ sight of the celebrity for a second before the crowd closed in.
gaps.explanation: catch sight of somebody/something means to notice them briefly.

gaps.sentence: He was exhausted because he had ___ the cooking for twenty people.
gaps.explanation: do the cooking is the fixed phrase; after 'had' the past participle 'done' is needed.
